chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who seeks from the Grace of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, what suffices his dependents, is greater in reward than the combatant in the Way of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for working to support one's family compared to jihad?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) elevates the mundane act of earning a halal livelihood to the status of jihad, emphasizing that the provider who secures sufficiency for their dependents attains a greater reward than the combatant in battle. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, underscores the Shia scholarly view that family sustenance is a primary religious duty (fard) and a form of worship, often prioritized over voluntary acts of struggle. It reflects the practical ethical framework of Shia jurisprudence, where financial responsibility is seen as a continuous, high-value spiritual endeavor.
